newsitem.title: UK: Gallup defends poll after UK party warning.
newsitem.headline: Gallup defends poll after UK party warning.

text.p: The Gallup polling organisation defended its survey methods on Thursday after Britain's opposition Labour party said caution should be exercised over the findings of its latest opinion poll.
"We have changed from face-to-face to telephone polling to make it more representative of the population," said Andy Brown, Gallup's research director.
He said the change in polling method would mean that raw figures collected would require less adjustment.
"I think you will find from the findings of this poll that the unadjusted figures are much closer to figures after they had been adjusted in previous face-to-face polls," he told Reuters.
The Gallup poll is due to be published in the Daily Telegraph newspaper on Friday.
In a statement, Labour said it had learned the poll would take a "totally new form".
"They (Gallup) have suddenly moved to random telephone sampling which may well show a significant shift from the previous month's findings," it said.
Labour said the poll should not compared with the December Gallup poll. The December Gallup 9000 poll showed it had a 30-point lead over the ruling Conservatives among voters.
The latest Gallup snapshot poll showed it had a 37-point lead. Other polls show Labour's lead is about 20 points.
